posts.name: Christopher
posts.cooked:
We certainly don’t expect it this time, as we aren’t really sure what to expect on the Kickstarter, day to day, but we definitely had a jump in the last two days of the Rook City Kickstarter.

Proof!

But I don’t know if that was indicative of the sorts of things that happen on Kickstarter, or just a fluke. Remember, this is just our second foray in the realm of Kickstarter, so the only expectation we had for this was that it would work - we wouldn’t have done it if we didn’t think it would work.

We certainly didn’t expect it to fully fund in a day. Or for the funding to double in under a week.

Or for us to be at over $80k in the last week.

We’re pretty much blown away by all this. So, thanks!

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked: Well, personally, I kickstart a lot of stuff. My standard practice when I see something interesting is to “star” it and then ignore it. As someone mentioned above, 48 hours before it ends, kickstarter sends me an email. Then I browse to the page, fully investigate the project, its pledge levels, and its stretch rewards and pledge appropriately if I’m interested. Obviously it was different for IR, which I pledged the very first day, but for most things I kickstart, I don’t pledge until the last 48 hours, so I would also expect a surge during that time. I’m not saying my practices are standard, but I’m sure at least SOME people do it the same.
